responsibilities: Data modelling & architecture: Build & create data models that help solve business problems. Follow team conventions and best practices for data architecture design. Understand Git workflows and raise PRs for review.

Semantic Layer & BI development: Define, build and edit semantic layer views that power customer-facing analytics such as User Apps, Dashboards, and AI tools. Create and build scalable and reusable dashboards.
Engineering collaboration & deployment: Understand the essentials of how analytics are surfaced within products. Participate in cross-team meetings and follow agreed deployment processes.

Commercial & stakeholder partnership: Understand the core commercial metrics and KPIs of the business. Respond to data requests from commercial teams. Build awareness of how data outputs are used in decision-making.

Team enablement & technical leadership: Seek support from senior colleagues, be curious and ask challenging questions. Share learnings with data peers. Follows established team processes and documentation standards.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: You will apply software engineering best practices—like version control, testing, and continuous integration—to the world of data warehousing.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: The JD emphasizes engineering rigour (version control, testing, CI, conventions, PR review) with no velocity/speed-focused language.
evidence.domain_risk: optimises more than 3 billion passenger journeys annually
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Public transport optimisation platform with large operational scale but no regulatory/financial-reporting language stated, so classified moderate.
evidence.data_team_maturity: In the Data Analytics team, we sit in the information layer between our tech stack and our customers
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: An existing Data Analytics team and 'Modern Data Information Layer' already exist and are being scaled, not built from zero.
evidence.jd_authorship: Define, build and edit semantic layer views that power customer-facing analytics such as User Apps, Dashboards, and AI tools.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Specific technical responsibilities (semantic layer views, Git workflows, PRs) show hiring-manager-level precision about what the role actually does.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Understand the core commercial metrics and KPIs of the business. Respond to data requests from commercial teams.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: A dedicated 'Commercial & stakeholder partnership' responsibility area centers the role's value on commercial metrics and customer-facing analytics.
evidence.autonomy_level: Seek support from senior colleagues, be curious and ask challenging questions. Follows established team processes
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Mixed: some ownership language ('Build & create data models') paired with execution/support framing ('Follow team conventions', 'Follows established team processes') typical of a mid-level role.
evidence.ai_role: power customer-facing analytics such as User Apps, Dashboards, and AI tools
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate builds semantic layer views and data models that power downstream AI tools — AI is a consumer of the candidate's data infrastructure.
evidence.testing_framing: Understand Git workflows and raise PRs for review... You know how to handle time-series anomalies, null values, and complex joins without breaking the pipeline.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Engineering rigour and pipeline reliability are framed as owned practices, not just listed tools.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: You know how to handle time-series anomalies, null values, and complex joins without breaking the pipeline.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Moderate: concern is about pipeline breakage and data quality rather than compliance or regulatory risk.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: You are building scalable data models that enable our platform to deliver real-time insights
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Mixed: building new scalable models within an existing information layer that is being scaled, not purely greenfield or purely fixing.
evidence.work_arrangement: Flexible working with hybrid working as the default in Ireland, core hours of 10am to 4pm, remote options depending on role
evidence.loss_aversion: Handling time-series anomalies, null values, and complex joins without breaking the pipeline reflects operational reliability concern rather than compliance risk — moderate.
